scope: Read-only CPU analysis of already completed N98 fixed100/150/200ps center files only
hypothesis: Saved point traces may distinguish local finite-window tail content from inconsistency among nominally matched run prefixes; neither outcome establishes the port gradient cause.
inputs: Use independently pinned original completed center checkpoints, FSP/H5/ports and frozen native/vendor code from verified temporal ancestry. No solver or optimizer entry point.
stages: Inventory enabled time_input/time_cavity/time_output data, t/coordinate axes, actual component names/shapes and monitor sampling/interpolation settings. Preserve unavailable fields as unavailable.
Enforce output/memory bounds before retrieving component arrays. Preserve absolute native times and units; do not resample silently.
For compatible grids compare shared prefixes, reporting absolute and normalized local field differences with denominators; separate numerical/settings variation from stochastic explanations.
Only after sampling/normalization review, analyze local late-time envelopes or raw point Fourier tails; do not equate them with flux/modal transmission or derivatives per nm.
stop_conditions: Missing/unusable/aliased or inconsistently sampled data: report limitation and review rather than invent trace information.
Changed input hashes or wrong ancestry: fail closed, preserving new attempt.
No automatic new FDTD duration ladder, adjoint pair or FOM replacement.
decision_after: If useful local tail data exist, assess whether a specific additional experiment can discriminate a stated cause. Do not assume quiet points rule out global effects.
A current-duration repeat can measure one repeat difference, not a universal noise floor.
Adjoint validation still requires the actual objective and reliable finite differences, with temporal endpoint, mesh, step-size and normalization limitations stated.
resource_budget: One scheduled CPU-only allocation if packet tests/review pass; verify shared GUI seats, queues and storage first. Runtime estimate must use actual extraction size; no guaranteed one-minute duration.
